data: Classical Physics: Energy and Force I

Dynamics is the study of the response of objects to applied forces. Motion has been a subject of philosophical investigations since the time of Aristotle. It took a very long time before its foundations were laid during the 18th century. In the process, the subject of calculus was formulated as the then existing mathematical framework was inadequate to succinctly express the empirical observations. Newton, who finally formalized the required notions to describe dynamics, encoded the known observations in three laws that bear his name. Two major themes that underlie the conceptual framework of dynamics are force and energy. Later developments proved Newton’s laws to be inaccurate at high speeds and small distances. How approximate are they? Landing on Mars at any specified location still relies on the predictions made using these laws. For many of our endeavours in science and engineering, these laws are fantastically accurate. An understanding of dynamics is essential to pursue any of the specialized topics in physics. Classical dynamics is possibly the beginning of both physics and mathematical analysis. Nevertheless, it continues to inspire new ideas in both subjects.
